label: TP
reason: Both alerts are True Positives. The XSS alert (L84-L85) reports taint flowing from getParameter to the HTML sink via concatenation into the filter string printed to the response writer. Although ESAPI.encodeForHTML is called on the entire filter string, the filter itself contains the raw user input ('|(uid=' + param)') which is not sanitized before being included in the LDAP filter syntax, allowing injection. The LDAP injection alert (L59) confirms the raw user parameter directly flows into the LDAP search filter without escaping special characters (like parentheses or braces), enabling LDAP injection attacks. Both sinks receive attacker-controlled data.

evidence.note: User parameter flows directly into LDAP filter string containing '(uid=' and '{0}' placeholders, enabling LDAP injection.
Raw filter string (containing unsanitized user input) is concatenated into HTML response output, causing XSS despite encodeForHTML call on the whole string.
